description: next/ v2.0 — Level-3 MOM OperationsRequest = the PLAN/target of manufacturing (B2MML OperationsRequest / ISA-95 Part 4). Opposite side to the OperationsResponse (the actuals). A Level-4 SalesOrder (SMProfile-CustomerOrder) TRIGGERS this L3 OperationsRequest; EXECUTED_AT a Machine (≡ EquipmentUnit level, consolidation 2026-07-15). v2.0: the order INSTANTIATES an OperationsDefinition (routing master) and decomposes per ProcessSegment into SegmentRequirements (HAS_SEGMENT_REQUIREMENT); temporal subdivisions (FO index) as Workorder (HAS_WORKORDER). Plan-vs-actual (qty_shortfall, late_delivery) is Cross-Source (it-evaluator), not a single-entity constraints block. --- 2026-08-13, CAPT-ORDER: absorbs the commercial projection of the withdrawn SMProfile-CustomerOrder (order_no, customer_ref, customer_name, total_amount, currency, due_date, quantity) and its FOR_CUSTOMER / FOR_ARTICLE edges. TRIGGERED_BY is removed: it had 0 edges in the live graph and its target profile is retired.

attributes.name: production_order_no
attributes.description: Join key — identity of the OperationsRequest. The OperationsResponse reports its actuals back via the same key (RESPONDS_TO).

attributes.name: sales_order_ref
attributes.description: Triggering Level-4 customer order (order_no, TRIGGERED_BY).

attributes.name: article_ref
attributes.description: Article to be manufactured (article_no, join key to Article).

attributes.name: machine_ref
attributes.description: Planned executing machine / line (machine_no). EXECUTED_AT Machine (machine_id).

attributes.name: department_ref
attributes.description: ERP department the order is routed to. Measured population 2026-08-03 on the live feed: SG | MECH | MONTAGE (LAGER and QMS exist in the ERP's department table but carry no orders on this projection). NOT declared as an enum: a plant may add a department without a schema change, and a consumer must never read an unknown department as 'no department'. WHY THIS ATTRIBUTE EXISTS: SMProfile-ShiftWindow (the plant calendar) is keyed by department_id, while the SSOT groups machines by ISA-95 location.area (sgm, cnc). Without a department on the order, a consumer can only ask the calendar the department-INDEPENDENT question 'does ANY department schedule this hour?' — enough to settle weekends, not enough to see that only SG runs a night shift. This attribute closes that join WITHOUT anyone guessing sgm->SG from name similarity. IT WAS NULL ON EVERY ROW UNTIL 2026-08-03, and the cause was upstream, not here: the ERP derives the department from erp.routing.work_center, which holds POOLS (POOL-SGM, POOL-CNC), while erp.machine_departments is keyed by INDIVIDUAL machine (sgm-01, cnc-01) — a LEFT JOIN that matched nothing and failed silently as NULL. sim-v5 6c6735f3 resolves the pool through erp.machine_pools.machine_ids; measured after: 4126/4126 released and 684/689 in-production orders carry a department. A consumer must still tolerate NULL — an order whose routing pool maps to no single department deliberately gets no answer rather than an arbitrary one.

attributes.name: qty_planned
attributes.description: Planned piece count (target). Counterpart to OperationsResponse.quantity_produced. Driver of the qty_shortfall rule.

attributes.name: planned_start_time
attributes.description: Planned START of the order's next non-terminal operation. Added 2026-07-31: the profile carried only planned_end_time, and a due date cannot order a queue — two orders due the same hour on the same machine had no defined sequence, so 'what runs next here' was unanswerable even where a machine WAS assigned. sim-v5 populates this from erp.order_operations.planned_start (100% populated on machine-assigned IN_PRODUCTION orders) via /api/orders.planned_start_time. Non-NULL only INSIDE the 24 h dispatch horizon; beyond it the order legitimately has no committed start yet.

attributes.name: planned_end_time
attributes.description: Planned completion date (target). Counterpart to actual_end_time. Driver of the late_delivery rule.

attributes.name: cycle_time_planned_sec
attributes.description: Planned cycle time per piece (s).

attributes.name: dispatch_sequence
attributes.description: 1-based position of this order in its machine's dispatch queue, inside the 24 h horizon. A total order down to (planned_start, production_order_no, operation_number), so ties are impossible. NULL beyond the horizon — capacity planning does not know the machine there yet, and a fabricated sequence would be worse than the pool. Together with planned_start_time this is what makes a shift-end projection possible: an ordered, machine-assigned sequence instead of a due-date heap.

attributes.name: parts_per_shot
attributes.description: Number of good parts ONE machine cycle yields — the mould's cavity count on injection-moulding machines, 1 on single-part machines. Added 2026-07-31 because it was published nowhere readable and had to be RECOVERED by dividing two part counters (measured 4 on sgm-001/005, 8 on sgm-004/006). MUST be read together with cycle_time_planned_sec, which is a time per SHOT: parts per hour = 3600 / cycle_time_planned_sec * parts_per_shot. Reading the shot time as a per-part time is exactly the defect fixed in golden-shift 0.3.0.

attributes.name: mould_ref
attributes.description: Identity of the mounted mould/tool that determines parts_per_shot (e.g. 'MOULD-PART-D-v1'). Travels with parts_per_shot because the cavity count is a property of the MOULD. NOTE: in sim-v5 the mould is mounted on the machine and machines are article-blind, so this varies per MACHINE, not per article.

attributes.name: material_ready_at
attributes.description: Time from which material is available — material-ready constraint.

attributes.name: customer_order_qty
attributes.description: Customer order quantity of the triggering order (denormalized).

attributes.name: customer_due_date
attributes.description: Customer delivery date of the triggering order (denormalized).

attributes.name: order_no
attributes.description: COMPATIBILITY KEY, adopted from the withdrawn SMProfile-CustomerOrder on 2026-08-13. Its value is the SAME STRING as production_order_no on every upstream row (measured: on 500/500 rows of /api/orders the four id fields order_id, auftrag_nr, kundenauftrag_nr and production_order_no are equal). It is NOT a second identity and MUST NOT be used as a merge key — kgIdProperty stays production_order_no. It exists solely so the consumers that read order_no today (view-engine order_reconciliation, deploy/scripts/kg-lineage-verify.sh, kg-legacy-purge.sh, it-evaluator's entity-label fallback) keep reading it after the CustomerOrder source is withdrawn. It writes order_no onto the 48.486 nodes that carry it today from the other side, so no consumer loses the field.

attributes.name: customer_ref
attributes.description: Customer of the triggering demand (kunde_id). Adopted from SMProfile-CustomerOrder 2026-08-13; the same column the withdrawn source read. FOR_CUSTOMER is built from it.

attributes.name: customer_name
attributes.description: Customer name (kunde_name). Adopted from SMProfile-CustomerOrder 2026-08-13. THIS SOURCE IS NOW THE ONLY WRITER: measured in the live KG, customer_name is set on 48.486 nodes and every one of them was written by the withdrawn erp-customer-orders binding. 100 % populated on the live feed.

attributes.name: total_amount
attributes.description: Order value (gesamtbetrag). Adopted from SMProfile-CustomerOrder 2026-08-13 — the driver of the EUR-impact ranking, read by it-evaluator pickImpactContext off the projected entity state (services/it-evaluator/src/evaluator.ts). Because that reader is entity-agnostic it keeps working unchanged once the field arrives on THIS profile. Fill rate measured on the live feed: 458/500 rows; 2.215 of the 48.486 order nodes carry no total_amount today, and that gap is upstream, not introduced here. unit_price is NOT adopted (see the source description): it is set on 0 nodes, so the quantity x unit_price fallback has never fired.

attributes.name: currency
attributes.description: Currency of total_amount (waehrung). Adopted from SMProfile-CustomerOrder 2026-08-13. Fill rate measured on the live feed: 461/500 rows.

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.description: Customer delivery commitment (lieferdatum_soll). Adopted from SMProfile-CustomerOrder 2026-08-13. READ THIS TOGETHER WITH planned_end_time: on this combined upstream projection BOTH map from lieferdatum_soll, so they carry the same value. That is the Sim's conflation of L4 and L3, faithfully reported rather than hidden — it is NOT evidence that the promise and the production target were separately planned. it-evaluator already coalesces due_date ?? planned_end_time, so the adoption changes no behaviour.

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.description: Ordered piece count (geplante_stueckzahl). Adopted from SMProfile-CustomerOrder 2026-08-13. Carries the SAME column as qty_planned and customer_order_qty — on this projection the order qty IS the customer qty. Kept under its old name because it-evaluator reads state['quantity'] directly for affected-quantity, and dropping the name would silence that reader.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Plan status of the OperationsRequest, as it reaches THIS profile through OUR source binding. VOCABULARY MEASURED 2026-07-12 against the full population of sim-v5 PROD (.154), not a sample and not the mapper's source code: the ERP contains 47.513 orders carrying exactly FIVE raw statuses — CANCELLED 21.676, INVOICED 19.827, IN_PRODUCTION 4.305, WAITING_PARTS 1.687, ON_HOLD 18. sources/rest/erp-production-orders.json binds /api/orders?exclude_status=CANCELLED,INVOICED,SHIPPED, so CANCELLED (-> storniert) and INVOICED (-> abgeschlossen) never arrive: 6.010 of 47.513 orders reach us, and the projection maps them onto exactly TWO canonical values — in_arbeit 4.305 (71,63 %) and freigegeben 1.705 (28,37 %, = WAITING_PARTS + ON_HOLD). THIS ENUM IS THE COMPLETE IMAGE, not a lower bound: the raw states that would be needed to produce any other value DO NOT EXIST IN THE ERP AT ALL. 'offen' requires raw DRAFT|PROPOSED|PLANNED and 'fertig' requires PRODUCED|COMPLETED — there is not ONE such row among all 47.513 (0,00 %); 'abgeschlossen' is reachable only from INVOICED, which our source excludes. Two earlier attempts got this wrong in opposite directions and BOTH were merged into this file's history: capt-qty-retire-shortfall measured the ENDPOINT and kept storniert+abgeschlossen (our own filter removes them); feat/ci-vocabulary-gate measured the PROJECTION's source code and kept offen+fertig+abgeschlossen (the raw states those branches need never occur, and its probe's 'fertig 1' is not reproducible — the true count is 0). The lesson is in the method: an enum must be measured where the data ENTERS US — endpoint AND source filter AND population — not at any one of the three. CONSEQUENCE: any `when` guard keying on 'offen' is structurally unsatisfiable and is a sleeping watchdog (this is why profiles/erp/customer-order.json#order_overdue is retired, and why ci/lint-vocabulary.mjs — which would have PASSED that guard against the fictional enum above — is only as honest as the enum it checks). Extend this enum ONLY against a fresh measurement of the full population. --- 2026-08-03, THE ENUM NOW COMES FROM THE PRODUCER'S CONTRACT, NOT FROM A SAMPLE. Chasing observed values one at a time was Sisyphus: the declared set was [freigegeben, in_arbeit], a paginated count added fertig (12) and abgeschlossen (5), and while I was committing that, `offen` appeared once. A live population moves; a vocabulary declared from a sample of it is stale by construction. sim-v5 declares the CLOSED set itself — packages/api-erp/src/shapes.ts:96, 'canonical DE: offen|freigegeben|in_arbeit|fertig|abgeschlossen|storniert'. That is the authority, and it is what is declared here. storniert is DELIBERATELY OMITTED: it is status_raw CANCELLED, which the exclude_status filter this source sends (CANCELLED,INVOICED,SHIPPED) removes, so it cannot arrive through THIS binding. The other five can. Raw mapping measured on the live feed: IN_PRODUCTION -> in_arbeit, WAITING_PARTS + ON_HOLD -> freigegeben, COMPLETED -> fertig, DELIVERED -> abgeschlossen. HOW THE TWO-VALUE DECLARATION SURVIVED SINCE 2026-07-12: the endpoint caps a page at 5000 rows and the FIRST page carries only in_arbeit/freigegeben, so a single unpaginated request CONFIRMS the wrong answer. It caught me too. All values beyond in_arbeit/freigegeben are TERMINAL or pre-release and change no behaviour: every consumer treats only in_arbeit and freigegeben as running (golden-shift ACTIVE_STATUSES, run-builder order-tracker, it-evaluator recipe-band-resolver). --- 2026-08-14, CAPT-FEED: storniert IS NOW REACHABLE AND IS THEREFORE DECLARED. The paragraph above omits it for exactly one reason -- 'it is status_raw CANCELLED, which the exclude_status filter this source sends removes, so it cannot arrive through THIS binding'. sources/rest/erp-production-orders.json v4.0.0 REMOVED that filter, so the premise is gone and the omission would now be a false statement about the feed. MEASURED the same day, /api/orders paged to exhaustion without the filter: 76.126 distinct orders, of which storniert 24.282 (31,9 %) -- the single largest status in the population, and previously 100 % invisible to us. The other four values were already declared and are unchanged (abgeschlossen 38.912, in_arbeit 8.062, freigegeben 4.870, fertig 2); 'offen' still does not occur (0 rows) and is kept only because the producer's own contract declares the closed set. BEHAVIOUR: storniert is TERMINAL and changes nothing downstream -- golden-shift ACTIVE_STATUSES, run-builder order-tracker and the it-evaluator recipe-band-resolver all treat only in_arbeit and freigegeben as running, so a cancelled order simply stops being active instead of being absent.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Order priority.

attributes.name: operations_definition_ref
attributes.description: v2.0 — instantiated routing (operations_definition_no, INSTANTIATES).

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.description: Last change. Server-managed and volatile on every read (sim-v5 returns a fresh value per GET), so promotion:never — kept in the snapshot but excluded from the change-trigger and never published on its own.

relationships.description: Moved here from SMProfile-CustomerOrder 2026-08-13 together with customer_ref. Built from kunde_id, which /api/orders serves on 100 % of rows.

Carried over from SMProfile-CustomerOrder 2026-08-13 so the 48.490 order->article edges measured in the live KG keep a producer. It duplicates PRODUCES from the same column; consolidating the two is a separate, provable decision and is NOT part of this change.
Consolidation 2026-07-15: Machine ≡ EquipmentUnit level, keyed machine_id — matches what the ERP source actually delivers (machine ids).
v2.0 — Inverse of SegmentRequirement.PART_OF: the target segments per ProcessSegment.
v2.0 — Inverse of Workorder.PART_OF: temporal subdivisions (FO index).

constraints.name: material_ready_after_planned_end
constraints.description: Material is not available until AFTER the order's own planned finish date. The ERP states BOTH dates on the same order, so this is a contradiction inside one record, not an estimate: an order planned to finish at T cannot be built from material the ERP says arrives after T. The IT/planning counterpart to the OT machine bands - a materials-planning finding about an order, not about a machine, and raised BEFORE the order runs late rather than after.
constraints.$comment: MEASURED 2026-08-31 by CAPT-ITLANE2 against the FULL production-order population of sim-v5 PROD (.154:38260 /api/orders, keyset-paginated over production_order_no, 17 pages): 84.229 distinct orders. (1) THE GUARD LITERALS ARE THE MEASURED VOCABULARY, not this profile's declared enum. The enum declares six values; the data carries exactly FOUR - abgeschlossen 43.010, storniert 25.859, in_arbeit 9.220, freigegeben 6.140. 'offen' and 'fertig' occur ZERO times, and a guard keyed on 'offen' is exactly how order_overdue on SMProfile-CustomerOrder became structurally unsatisfiable. The two literals above are both measured present. (2) POPULATION AND HIT RATE. material_ready_at is written on 9.220 of 84.229 rows, and on in_arbeit rows ONLY (9.220 of 9.220 in_arbeit); everywhere else the attribute is absent and the tri-state predicate reads 'unknown', never 'ok'. Of the 9.220 eligible orders, 10 carry material_ready_at LATER than planned_end_time: 0,11 % of the eligible set, 0,012 % of the population. A minority and a workable worklist - not a log storm. (3) WHY NOT THE OBVIOUS RULE. 'Open order past its due date' was measured in the same run and is NOT viable: 7.485 of 15.360 open orders are past lieferdatum_soll - 48,73 % of the open book, median 24 days over. A rule half the population violates describes the backlog, it does not find anything. It is also $now-keyed, and a $now constraint pins EVERY tracked entity against it-evaluator's idle eviction (ENTITY_EVICT_IDLE_MS), so it would hold all 84.229 orders in the working set for ever. This rule compares two attributes of the same record and is therefore evictable. (4) LANE. it-evaluator publishes domain='it'; the engine anchors an IT episode on about_order_no and sets NO about_machine_id (engine.ts constraintRaisedLocked). With concern=operations, mom_category=production and no deviation_class, laneOf returns 'it' - which is the point: the second living rule in a lane that had exactly one against OT's 22.

isa95.note: Level-3 MOM OperationsRequest (B2MML) = PLAN/target. v2.0: the earlier flat SegmentRequirement.MaterialRequirement projection (propertyMap) is now modeled out as a dedicated SMProfile-SegmentRequirement per ProcessSegment (HAS_SEGMENT_REQUIREMENT); the order INSTANTIATES an OperationsDefinition and can be subdivided via Workorder (FO index). article_ref/machine_ref remain a denormalized header shortcut. Plan-vs-actual = Cross-Source reconcile, not a constraints block. QUANTITY: qty_planned is optional and is omitted for continuous bulk/length-based goods (e.g. continuous web/strand goods, sold by length) — then only times/status drive the PLAN. --- 2026-08-13, CAPT-ORDER: the Level-4 SalesOrder side is NO LONGER MODELLED AS A SEPARATE ENTITY. The upstream serves one row per order under four identical id fields and no distinct customer-order number, so a second entity on the same id was a duplication, not a level separation — it produced 48.486 double-labelled nodes and 48.485 TRIGGERS SELF-LOOPS. The commercial attributes of the demand (customer, value, currency, promised date, ordered qty) now live here as denormalised attributes of the OperationsRequest, which is what the data supports. A genuine L4/L3 separation requires sim-v5 to serve real, separately-keyed customer orders; that is a data-model project against the live sim and is filed as a backlog item, not attempted here.
